who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane L9a (lints and diagnostics) of the front-end-on-memo port
task: Port blaze-lints, blaze-diagnostics, blaze-macro-eval and the small tool crates from blaze-query to blaze-memo
do: (1) Attach sites are one ast-grep rule, run on the lane's crates only: `ast-grep run --lang rust --pattern 'blaze_query::db::attach($DB, $F)' --rewrite 'blaze_memo::attach($DB, $F)' --update-all crates/blaze-lints crates/blaze-diagnostics crates/blaze-macro-eval crates/blaze-ext-host crates/blaze-doc crates/blaze-shader crates/blaze-diff-mir crates/span crates/intern crates/blaze-fmt` (85 matches; a call inside a fixture's text is not matched and is edited by hand). (2) Other rules used: `store_marks($DB, $O, ())` -> `store_marks($DB, $O)` (2), `let $N = db.nonce_and_revision();` -> `let $N = blaze_memo::Database::memo(db).snapshot_epoch();` (4, one put back by hand where the nonce is read), `Cancelled::WouldWaitOnItself { asked: None }` -> `Cancelled::GaveWay` (1), `blaze_query::carry(blaze_query::Carried::word($T, $P))` -> `blaze_graph::sched::carry(blaze_graph::sched::Carried::word($T, $P))` (1). A type such as `(Nonce, blaze_query::db::View)` is parsed as an expression by a pattern and matches nothing: edit it by hand. (3) A value that is a flat list, set or map of Copy rows becomes `crate::kept` (`kept::slice`, `kept::text`, `kept::Map`/`kept::Set`: rows sorted by the key's `FixedState` hash and searched, since most front-end ids are not `Ord`); a value that is a tree (diagnostics, nested lists, summaries) keeps its heap type and the query is `owns`. (4) An `#[interned]` key whose field owns memory (a `Conf`, a profile `Loaded`, a `Disallowed`) becomes a plain `Copy` struct holding `intern::Interned<T>` with `#[derive(blaze_memo::Home)]` and `#[home(skip)]`, `intern::impl_internable!(T)` once, and the old `new(_db, ..)`/accessor names kept so callers do not change. (5) Strings inside kept rows become `intern::Symbol`. (6) Cycle fallbacks lose their `Id` argument. (7) Lints that recognise the engine by crate name (`error_debug`, `lock_across_query`, `query_in_loop`) and their fixtures name `blaze_memo`/`blaze_memo_macros`.
why: The lint and diagnostic queries are many small crate indexes and body queries; one recipe per value shape keeps the port mechanical and the ratcheted `owns` count small.
